Definition: from a compound of G2095 and G3056; to speak well of, i.e. (religiously) to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper):--bless, praise.
BiblicalUsage: The word eulogéō carries the sense of bless, praise. In Matthew 14:19, the text says "he blessed." In Mark 6:41, the text says "and blessed."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that eulogéō matters because worship is not a performance but a response — we answer what God has done with what we are. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Feeding of the Five Thousand; Triumphal Entry; Mary Visits Elizabeth
